# drot

> Applies a plane rotation.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import drot from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/drot';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
drot( N, x, strideX, y, strideY, c, s ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `x` stride length |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | `y` stride length |
| `c` | `number` | Cosine of the angle of rotation |
| `s` | `number` | Sine of the angle of rotation |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: output array

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
drot.strided( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY, c, s ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of indexed elements |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · First input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `x` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Second input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | `y` stride length |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` |
| `c` | `number` | Cosine of the angle of rotation |
| `s` | `number` | Sine of the angle of rotation |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `y`

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `drot()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`DROT`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/drot.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import drot from './../lib/base.js';

// Apply a Givens rotation to vectors x and y:
const x = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );
const y = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 5.0, 6.0 ] );

drot( 3, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0, 0.8, 0.6 );
console.log( x ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( y ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `DROT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DROT applies a plane rotation.

### Further Details

jack dongarra, linpack, 3/11/78. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>
